title: Prove exponential parity-prefix growth above tail one (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with finite controls: the exact triangular parity compiler can have exponential proper-prefix amplification for **every fixed real eta>1**, despite a completed forward norm bounded independently of dimension.

```text
a = (eta+1)/2 > 1, b = a-1, f(z) = 1+bz+az^2
||T_N(f)||_infinity = 1+eta
||first right-shear prefix||_infinity = a^(N/2-1)
```

Together with Brian's cited #4737 theorem at eta<=1, this makes one the sharp threshold for uniform forward macro-prefix control over the complete tail-budget class. The new result is the exponential family above one. No new kappa, supplier admission or multiplication theorem is claimed. The selected frontier stays unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: #4737 supplies a single eta=2 counterexample to extending its cap. After: a geometric-series proof supplies exponential growth for every eta>1, on a three-term nonnegative symbol. An explicit bounded input attains the norm. For eta=3 and N=16, the prefix norm is exactly 128 while the completed norm is 4.

Local warning-strict normal and optimized verification each pass all 25 exact rational fixtures and seven controls through N=64. Every fixture compares the root factorization's entire matrix to its literal Toeplitz endpoint, checks both shear inverse orders and an attaining input. Each registered command takes under one second locally; the registered replay takes about 1.4 seconds. These timings establish timeout headroom, not a performance improvement. Generated JSON receipts bind every package file by SHA256. No receipt is hand-authored.

From the repository root, CPython 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/triangular-parity-tail-threshold
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/triangular-parity-tail-threshold/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/triangular-parity-tail-threshold/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/triangular-parity-tail-threshold --check-source-history
```

Expected marker: `PASS_PARITY_TAIL_THRESHOLD fixtures=25 controls=7 max_n=64 no_new_kappa`.

## Limitations

The all-real-eta conclusion is a written scoped proof; finite rational fixtures corroborate it. The obstruction is specific to this parity factorization at completed-shear boundaries. The family is not claimed to have a uniformly bounded inverse endpoint. The retained eta<1 theorem and its actual caller are not contradicted. Rounded FFT/shear gates, alternate compilers, Gaussian integration, precision/tape costs, native admission, Lean, Docker and selected full replay remain outside scope and unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

The package pins Brian's forward theorem and Vlado Vojdanovski/Cinna Davis's compiler as historical sources. Credit also Brian #4731, James Reed #4699 and the finite lineage, Ryanson Jonathan and unpaidmoon #4371. No predecessor executable or result is audited. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Open next questions

- Can a changed factorization avoid this amplification when the endpoint and inverse endpoint are separately bounded? Start with a specified zero-free symbol and its even-part zero; no such class is constructed here.
- Can one caller afford normalization into near-identity factors after coefficient generation, storage and extra shears are all charged? Start with the caller's literal symbol and complete invoice.
